intervention: oracle: cut the cell arm at the rank of the last gold cell
note: a CEILING, not a method -- it reads gold. It keeps the distractors that outrank gold (no policy can drop those) and removes only the tail.

P1.verdict: PASS on HiTab, OVERSHOT on AIT-QA

P2.measured: identical to four decimals on both (.5499, .7892)
P2.verdict: PASS -- retrieval untouched, so this is pure precision

P4.stated: the bigger token cut gains more
P4.measured: HiTab cut 63% and gained .025; AIT-QA cut 43% and gained .091
P4.verdict: FAIL -- and the reason is this session's own finding: what matters is TABLES, not tokens. AIT-QA shed 4 whole tables (10.51 -> 6.49), HiTab S3c barely one (2.56 -> 1.62).

verdict: First row of the decision table on AIT-QA (+.0909 >= +.05), second row on HiTab (+.0253). Build the predictor.
why_it_matters: +.0909 on AIT-QA is the largest single gain anything in this repo has produced there since the title, and unlike every OSC-raising intervention it CONVERTED: p is 0.0 at 53:12.
It recovers 15.8% of AIT-QA's goldcell gap and 8.9% of HiTab's, at zero cost to completeness -- the wall the table cap hit.
It confirms the direction the ceilings pointed at: the axis is precision, not recall. Adding material has failed every time; removing the tail works.
what_the_predictor_has_to_do: estimate k*(q) = the rank of the last gold cell, from retrieval signal alone. Under-estimating costs OSC (the oracle never does), so the policy needs a margin tuned on train. NEXT.md names the features: top-1 score, top1-top2 gap, top-k variance, agreement between the two retrievers.
